FOREWORD This lndian Standard (Part 3/See 2) (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Fertilizers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. Number of standards in the area of fertilizers comprising methods of sampling and test and products have been formulated: international Organization for Standardization (1S0) has also published a number of standards on the methods of sampling and test. Keeping in view the globalization trends the Committee decided to align lndian Standards on test methods for fertilizers with International (1S0) Standards to the extent possible. This standard covers test methods, which have been retained from the first revision, for which no corresponding International Standards are available. The Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is seized with the need to align these test methods with International Standards as and when they are available.

IS 6092 (Part 3/See 2) :2004

Indian Standard METHODS OF SAMPLING AND TEST FOR FERTILIZERS
PART 3 DETERMINATION Section 2 Test Methods OF PHOSPHORUS Not Covered Under Dual Number Standards

(Second Revision)
1 SCOPE This standard (Part 3/See 2) prescribes methods for testing of phosphorus in its various forms in fertilizers, including fertilizer mixtures. The standard covers methods for which no corresponding International Standard is presently available. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions, which through reference in this text constitute the provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreement based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below:
IS No. Title

5 SELECTION OF TEST METHOD AND PREPARATION OF SAMPLE SOLUTION 5.1 General Methods of determination of total phosphates, water soluble phosphates, citrate soluble phosphates, citrate insoluble phosphates, citric acid soluble phosphates, and free phosphoric acid have been described separately. These methods are applicable to straight as well as mixed phosphatic fertilizers. 5.1.1 Three methods have been prescribed determination of phosphorus, namely: for

a) Quinoline phosphomolybdate gravimetric method [see.IS 6092 (Part 3/See 4)]; b) Alkalimetric quinolinium molybdophosphate method; and c) Spectrophotometric molybdovanado phosphate method. Out of these the first one gravimetric [see IS 6092 (Part 3/See 4)] shall be the referee method in case of any dispute. 5.2 Preparation of Sohtion of Sample

3 SAMPLING AND PREPARATION OF SAMPLE FOR ANALYSIS Representative test sample of fertilizer shall be prepared and drawn as prescribed in IS 6092 (Part 1). 4 QUALITY OF REAGENTS Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be used in tests.
NOTE -- `Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities, which affect the results of analysis.

5.2.2.1

Treat 1 g of the prepared sample by the following methods depending on the nature of the sample: a)
Suitable for materials containing small quantities of organic matter -- Dissolve in

30 ml of concentrated nitric acid and 5 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid and boil slowly (in a fume chamber) until organic matter is destroyed. b)
Suitable for fertilizers containing large quantities of iron or aluminiumphosphate and for basic slag -- Dissolve in 15 to 30 ml of

percent perchloric acid. Boil very gently until solution is colorless or nearly so and white dense fumes appear in the flask. Do not boil to dryness at any time. With sample containing large quantities of organic matter, temperature should be raised to i%ming point (approximately 170�C) over a period of at least 1 h. Cool slightly, add 50 ml of water and boil for a few minutes.
CAUTION-- Perchloricacid may cause explosion in contact with organic matter and must not therefore be added unless most of the organic matteris oxidized with boiling nitric acid. Avoid direct contact with perchloric acid. AH digestion must be carried out in fume chamber with fool proof suction/ ventilation device.

concentrated hydrochloric acid and 3 to 10 ml ofconcentrated nitric acid and boil till finning. cool.
NOTE -- For hydroscopic fertilizers it is preferableto use electric mixer/blender.

c)

Suitable for organic materials like oil cake, bone meal, jlsh meal, cottonseed meal alone or in mixtures -- Evaporate with 5 ml of

magnesium nitrate solution on steam bath, dry thoroughly, ignite to destroy organic matter and dissolve in 1:1 mixture of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid (warm, if necessary) when cool, dilute to volume. d)
Generally applicable to materials or mtitures containing large quantities of organic matter-- Boil with 20 to 30 ml of concentrated

Alternatively, the sample can be directly digested in 20 to 25 ml of triacid mixture (nitric-perchloricsulphuric in the ratio of 10:4: 2) in 100 to 150 ml Kjeldahl flask starting with a low heat till dense fhmes of perchloric acid appear. Soluble silica (SiOJ in the extract interferes with phosphate estimations. In digestion with perchloric/sulphuric acid, it gets dehydrated and becomes insoluble and can be easily filtered off. In hydrochloric acid digest, if soluble silica is expected, this can be dehydrated and thoroughly baked on a sand bath, re-extracted in hydrochloric acid and separated by filtration. 5.2.2.2 Cool the digest obtained in 5.2.2.1, trahsfer to a 250-ml volumetric flask, dilute to the mark, mix and filter through dry filter discarding the first few millilitre of the filtrate. Use the filtrate for the tests as specified. 6 TOTAL PHOSPHORUS 6.1 Spectrophotometric Method 6.1.1 General This method determines ortho-phosphate content of a properly prepared solution. This method is not recommended for materials yielding coloured solution or solution containing ions other than ortho-phosphate which form coloured cdmplex with molybdovanadate. Citrate or excessive amount of chloride interfere by suppressing the colour development. 6.1.2 Apparatus 6.1.2.1 Spectrophotometer -- Any commercially available model of proven performance with stray light filter and matched 1-1.5 cm cells. Means for dispelling heat from light source and avoiding voltage fluctuations in the current supply, are to be ensured. 6.L3 Reagents
6.1.3.1 A401ybdovana&te reagent -- Dissolve 40 g of

sulphuric acid in a 200-ml long neck flask, adding 2 to 4 g of sodium nitrate or potassium nitrate at the beginning of the digestion and a small quantity of the nitrate after the solution is nearly colorless. When the solution is colorless, cool, add 150 ml of water and boil for a few minutes. Before adding sodium nitrate or potassium nitrate, let the mixture digest, at gentle heat, if necessary, until violence of reaction is over.
NOTE -- If the sample contains large amount of calcium, the productionof insoluble calcium sulphate in the sulphuric acid digest may create problems, it is better to follow the proceduregiven in 5.2.2 .l(e).

One millilitre of this solution is equivalent to 1 mg of P20j. 6.2.1.3 Standard nitric acid solution -- Prepare nitric acid solution equivalent to molar concentration of standard sodium hydroxide solution and standardize by titrating against it using phenolphthalein. Using only a jet of water, transfer the precipitate and pad to precipitation flask and breakup the pad with a jet of water. 6.2.2.2 Transfer an aliquot of the sample solution containing 20 to 30 mg of PzO~and not more than 5 ml of concentrated acid, to 500-ml conical flask, add 20 ml of 10 percent citric acid solution, and adjust to about 100 ml. Add 60 ml of quimociac reagent, immediately cover with watch glass and place on medium temperature hot plate. After the solution comes to boiling point, move to cooler portion of hot plate and boil gently for one minute. Let it cool until flask can be handled comfortably with bare hand. Allow the precipitate to settle down. 6.2.2.3 Prepare a uniform pulped-paper pad about 5 mm thick on perforated porcelain disc in a funnel (60�) fitted on a suction flask by adding not less than 2 approximately equal increments of water suspension of pulped paper and sucking dry with vacuum between additions. Ensure that the setting is leak proof. Swirl the flask, pour contents on to the filter and wash the flask five times with 15 ml portions of water adding washings to funnel. Immediately after funnel has emptied, wash down sides with about 15 ml of water to remove residual acetone, which causes excessively fast drying and later lump formation if allowed to evaporate. 7.3 Extraction of Water Soluble Phosphorus 7.3.1 Place in a funnel 1 g of accurately weighed

IS 6092 (Part 3/See 2): 2004 prepared sample on a 9-cm filter paper in a fimnel and wash with small portions of water until the filtrate measures approximately 250 ml. Add freshly distilled water in fine stream directed around entire periphery of filter paper in circular path, ensuring that water and solids are thoroughly mixed with each addition. Let each portion pass through the filter before adding more; use mild suction if washing would not otherwise be complete in about 1 h. Ensure complete extraction of P20~ (washing should be free of soluble phosphates). Add 20 to 25 ml of nitric acid to the washings and boil for 15-20 min to hydrolyze non-orthophosphates. Dilute to 250 ml and mix. Preserve the residue for other tests. 7.4 Determination 7.4.1 Volumetric Method

the paper is reduced to pulp while occasionally relieving pressure by removing the stopper momentarily. Continuously agitate the contents of the stoppered flask in an apparatus equipped to hold the contents of the flask in a thermostatic controlled water bath at 65�C. The arrangement should be such that entire inner surface of the flask and the stopper are continuously bathed with the solution. Exactly 1 h after adding the filter paper and the residue, remove the flask from the apparatus and immediately filter the contents by suction as rapidly as possible. Using a filter paper (Whatman No. 5 or equivalent), in a Buchner funnel, wash with water maintained at 65�C until volume of the filtrate is approximately 350 ml, allowing time for thorough draining before adding more water. If the material yields a cloudy filtrate, wash a few times with 5 percent ammonium nitrate solution. 8.2.2 Determine phosphorus in the citrate insoluble residue by one of the following methods: a) Transfer the filter paper and residue, to a porcelain or silica crucible, dry and ignite until all organic matter is destroyed. Digest with 10 to 15 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid and 3 ml of concentrated nitric acid until all phosphates dissolve. Cool and dilute to a known volume. Treat the wet filter and contents with the method prescribed in 5.2.2.l(a), (c), (d) or (e). Dilute the solution to 250 ml or suitable volume, mix well, filter through dry filter paper and determine P20, as in IS 6092 (Part 3/See 4) or in 6.2. 10.2.4 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid -- Dilute 250 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid with water to 1 Iitre. 10.3 Preparation of Solution

11.1.2 Standard Sodium Hydroxide Solution -- 0.1 N.
11.1.3 Bromocreso[ Green Indicator Solution --

Weigh exactly 5 g of the prepared sample and transfer to a stoppered bottle of about one litre capacity. Separately dissolve 10 g of citric acid in water, dilute to 500 ml and adjust the temperature to 20"C. Add this solution to the sample in the bottle, shaking so as to avoid caking. Shake the bottle continuously in an end on mechanical for exactly 30 min. Pour the whole of the liquid at once on to a large medium fine filter and collect the filtrate. If the filtrate is not clear, pass it again through the same filter. Reject first few portions of the filtrate. 10.4 Procedure Transfer a volume of the solution prepared as in 10.3 containing not more than 25 mg P20~ to a 500-ml conical flask. Dilute the solution with water to 100 ml. If the sample does not contain calcium, add 100 to 200 mg of calcium carbonate. Then add dilute sodium hydroxide solution dropwise until a faint permanent turbidity or precipitate is formed. Dissolve the precipitate by dropwise addition of dilute hydrochloric acid, but avoid an excess. Then proceed with the determination of P205 by the method prescribed in IS 6092 (Part 3/See 4), 6.1 and 6.2. 11 FREE PHOSPHORIC
11.1 Reagents ACID

Dissolve 0.1 g of bromocresol green in 100 ml of rectified spirit or ethyl alcohol (95 percent). 11.2 Procedure Weigh accurately about 2.0 g of the prepared sample into a 250-ml Erlenmeyer flask. Add 100 ml of acetone (check/adjust for neutrality). Fix to a wrist action shaker. Shake for 1 h. 11.2.1 Filter through rapid (Whatman No. 4 or equivalent) filter paper into 250-m I Erlenmeyer flask. Wash with four 10 ml portions of acetone. Evaporate acetone as far as possible. Add about 50 ml water and 3 to 4 drops of bromocresol green indicator. Titrate with standard sodium hydroxide solution, until the colourjust changes from yellow to blue. 11.3 Calculation Free phosphoric acid (as P,O,), ~ ~~ ~ ~ ~ -- percent by mass M where

Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'.
